title: Catalonia and the east
subtitle: Cava, Priorat and Monastrell
objectives: Name the main wines of the Levante

steps.title: Cava and Penedès
steps.body: Most Cava comes from Penedès, near Barcelona, made by the traditional method. The main grapes are Macabeo, Xarel-lo and Parellada. Minimum ageing on lees is 9 months; Reserva needs 18 months and Gran Reserva 30. Some producers left the Cava DO to form Corpinnat and Clàssic Penedès, with stricter rules.

steps.title: Priorat
steps.body: Priorat, south-west of Barcelona, revived in the late 1980s when a group of producers, including René Barbier and Álvaro Palacios, made powerful reds from old Garnacha and Cariñena. Vines grow on steep slopes of llicorella, a dark slate that forces roots deep and keeps yields tiny. It became a DOCa in 2000.
steps.highlight: Llicorella slate, old Garnacha and Cariñena

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its grapes.
steps.explanation: Each region of eastern Spain has its own grape identity.

steps.title: The Levante
steps.body: South of Valencia, the Levante is hot and dry. Jumilla and Yecla make ripe, powerful reds from Monastrell, the same grape as Mourvèdre. Alicante makes reds and a rare sweet wine, Fondillón. Valencia makes everything from bulk wine to sweet Moscatel.

steps.prompt: Priorat's llicorella is a dark slate soil.
steps.explanation: Yes. It forces roots deep and keeps yields very low, giving concentrated wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cava is mostly from Penedès, made by the traditional method
Priorat grows old Garnacha and Cariñena on llicorella slate
The Levante makes ripe Monastrell reds
